The Tamaulipas state government is expanding the Planta Potabilizadora Norte, the North Water Treatment Plant, in Nuevo Laredo, a project aimed at improving the drinking water supply for the border city, according to the state government.

The work is being carried out through the state Secretariat of Public Works, known as the SOP, with an investment of more than 84 million pesos, according to the announcement released Friday, Nov. 6.

Secretary of Public Works Pedro Cepeda Anaya said the expansion will modernize the plant's facilities and add the infrastructure needed to strengthen the water purification process, improving the plant's operating capacity.

The work includes the pumping station, flocculator, sedimentation tank, filters, clear-water tanks, piping, chlorination building and electrical work, along with asphalt paving, sidewalks, curbs, walls and cattle guards, according to the state.

Cepeda Anaya said the project is part of the state government's actions to address the basic needs of Tamaulipas families and improve public services.

Sources: Gobierno del Estado de Tamaulipas.
